title: Unencrypted Data Transmission
description: Parent User (EE1) sends registration data (email, password, name, govt ID, six-digit code) to Authentication Service (P1) without encryption, exposing sensitive personal information.

title: Unauthorized Data Access
description: Authentication Service (P1) processes registration data without proper access controls, allowing unauthorized entities to access sensitive user information.

title: Data Disclosure
description: The Authentication Service (Process P1) is transferring parent account data to the MongoDB users collection (DataStore DS1). This constitutes a data disclosure as the process is explicitly transferring personal data across a boundary to a data store.

title: Data Disclosure
description: The MongoDB users collection (DataStore DS1) is receiving parent account data from the Authentication Service (Process P1). This constitutes a data disclosure as the data store is receiving personal data from a process.

title: Unauthorized Access to JWT
description: Process P1 (Authentication Service) may expose JWT tokens to unauthorized external entities (EE1) without proper validation or encryption, leading to potential token theft or replay attacks.

title: Data Leakage of User Data
description: Process P1 may leak sensitive user data (e.g., PII) to the parent user (EE1) without appropriate access controls or data masking, violating privacy principles.

title: Unauthorized Access to Child User Data
description: External entity EE2 (Child User) may attempt to access or retrieve data from the Authentication Service P1 without proper authorization, potentially leading to privacy violations.

title: Unauthorized Data Access by Child User
description: Process P1 (Authentication Service) may be accessed by External entity EE2 (Child User) in a way that allows unauthorized data retrieval or modification.

title: Unauthorized Access to JWT
description: Process P1 (Authentication Service) may expose JWT (userType child) to unauthorized external entities (EE2) without proper validation or encryption, leading to potential unauthorized access to user identity information.
assumptions: No explicit validation or encryption is mentioned in the flow description.
uncertainty_note: Uncertain if JWT is always encrypted or validated before being exposed to EE2.

title: Unauthorized Data Access from Process
description: External Entity EE2 may access data stored in Process P1 (Authentication Service) without authorization, potentially accessing sensitive user profiles or other data.
assumptions: No explicit authorization mechanism is mentioned for EE2 to access P1's data.
uncertainty_note: Uncertain if EE2 has any defined access controls or permissions to P1.

title: Profile Creation via Linking
description: External Entity EE1 (Parent User) initiates a data flow to Process P3 (Child Profile Management) to create a child profile. This flow involves the collection of quasi-identifiers (name, DOB, gender, govt ID) which, when combined with the parent's identity, allows for the creation of a unique user profile. This constitutes a linking interaction where the combination of attributes reveals additional information about the data subject.
assumptions: The system requires the creation of a child profile to track user activity or demographics.

title: Profile Creation via Linking
description: Process P3 (Child Profile Management) initiates the data flow to External Entity EE1 (Parent User) to create a child profile. This flow involves the collection of quasi-identifiers (name, DOB, gender, govt ID) which, when combined with the parent's identity, allows for the creation of a unique user profile. This constitutes a linking interaction where the combination of attributes reveals additional information about the data subject.
assumptions: The system requires the creation of a child profile to track user activity or demographics.

title: Child Profile Disclosure
description: Process P3 (Child Profile Management) directly transfers child profile data to DataStore DS2 (MongoDB childprofiles collection). This constitutes a data disclosure (D) as the process explicitly transfers personal data across a boundary to a data store.

title: Child Profile Disclosure
description: DataStore DS2 (MongoDB childprofiles collection) directly transfers child profile data to Process P3 (Child Profile Management). This constitutes a data disclosure (D) as the data store explicitly transfers personal data across a boundary to a process.

title: Unauthorized Video Search

title: Inappropriate Video Search

title: Non-compliant Video Search

title: Data Leakage in Search

title: User Error in Search

title: Improper Personal Data Management

title: Data Disclosure

title: Data Disclosure

This constitutes a data disclosure as the process is explicitly transferring personal data (child search and watch history) to a third party (the data store).

title: Data Disclosure
description: Transfer of child browsing data from MongoDB (DataStore) to AI Recommendation Engine (Process). This constitutes a data disclosure as personal data is being moved across a boundary to a third party.
assumptions: The data transfer is intended and by design.

title: Data Disclosure
description: Transfer of child browsing data from MongoDB (DataStore) to AI Recommendation Engine (Process). This constitutes a data disclosure as personal data is being moved across a boundary to a third party.
assumptions: The data transfer is intended and by design.

title: Data Disclosure to Third-Party Advertisers
description: The AI Recommendation Engine (Process P4) is transferring browsing data to Third-Party Advertisers (ExternalEntity EE3). This constitutes a data disclosure as the system is transferring personal data to a known third party without explicit consent or a modeled flow between the external entity and the process.

title: Data Disclosure from Third-Party Advertisers
description: The Third-Party Advertisers (ExternalEntity EE3) are receiving browsing data from the AI Recommendation Engine (Process P4). This represents a data disclosure where the external entity is receiving personal data from a system it does not control.

title: Data Disclosure
description: Government ID images are being transferred from the Authentication Service (Process P1) to the File System (DataStore DS4). This constitutes a direct data disclosure as the system is transferring personal data (government ID images) to a third-party data store.

title: Data Disclosure
description: The File System (DataStore DS4) is storing government ID images. While the store itself is not the originator of the data flow, the act of storing this specific personal data creates a risk of disclosure if the store is accessed or if the data is inadvertently shared with other systems.

title: JWT Storage in localStorage
description: The Authentication Service (P1) stores a JWT in the browser's localStorage. This action creates a potential privacy threat because the JWT, which contains sensitive user credentials, is now stored in a client-side storage mechanism accessible to the browser. This storage can be accessed by the browser or other client-side applications, potentially exposing the user's identity and access tokens.
assumptions: The JWT is a standard security token used for authentication.

title: JWT Storage in localStorage
description: The DataStore (DS5) is storing a JWT in its internal storage. This is an invalid interaction according to the mapping table, as data stores do not directly exchange data without a process. The threat arises at the element that receives the data (the browser), where the data can be processed or stored in a way that causes a privacy threat.
assumptions: The JWT is a standard security token used for authentication.

title: Child Profile Linking
description: Process P3 retrieves child profile data and associates it with the parent User (EE1) for review. This linking of child data to the parent entity may reveal additional information about the child's history or attributes, potentially compromising privacy if the parent's review process is sensitive or if the data is shared with parties not intended to see the full profile.
assumptions: The parent User (EE1) has access to the retrieved child profile data.

title: Parent User Linking
description: External Entity EE1 (Parent User) receives and processes the retrieved child profile data. The act of processing this data and potentially using it for review or decision-making constitutes a linking activity that could expose sensitive child history information.
assumptions: The parent User (EE1) has access to the retrieved child profile data.
